differences.what: The flat top now has real two-row openings, corner pinnacles, a checker band and five colonnettes dividing six upper windows.
The south bow has three basement lights, three principal transom openings and four second-storey sashes; the north loggia has paired Ionic columns and a pierced lower panel.

T-2565's loggia, compared at this view's scale (T-2577): Glessner's front and the tree in front of 1808 hide the loggia; only the top of the balcony's south pedestal shows, so this view cannot judge its carving or columns.

T-2566's granite, compared at this view's scale (T-2577): the tree's crown covers the front's checker band and courses and Glessner's roof hides the bow; the north return's courses are T-2564's item above.
Hidden rear elevations and concealed roof surfaces cannot be accepted from this front photograph.
The earlier low stone boundary replaces the generic iron fence with urns. Its exact post/rail sections remain reconstructed.

T-2564: the north return is laid in large dressed courses (about 0.46 m) with staggered joints, 5.5 m long as the course counts in the 1887-89 and 1948 views give it, where it was a smooth 2.8 m slab.
The original is monochrome; granite colour is not shown. Sepia/scan casts are not material colour.

T-2578 ruling: the stone parapet stops at the rear pinnacle. Every picture that sees that corner (1887, Taylor 2135, the 1888 Glessner plate, the c. 1888 view looking SW, the Glessner front, 1948) shows sky straight behind it, or in 1948 a darker wall about a course lower; the model drops it there.

T-2577: the cornice box under the lattice is laid in the front's dressed stone, so the crown reads as one stone mass from the wall head to the lattice, as the photographs show it; the brown band is gone in this render.
T-2578: the cowl ventilator this view shows over the return is built, at the place along the return it shows (about 0.58 of the return in both).

T-2578: the ventilator's cap stands higher over the coping in this print than in the render; this camera's residual or the cap's reconstructed set-back behind the face (T-2579's re-fitted cameras decide which). T-2713: ruled through the re-fitted camera, not this one. This camera (T-1883's fit) cannot judge the cap's height: it puts the rear pinnacle about 60 px right of and 40 px below the photograph's (x 1366, y 170 against 1307, 130), so the return's run and fall over the coping are its own. Read through T-2579's re-fitted camera on the 1888 Glessner plate, the cap's top stood 3.5 px (0.1 m) beyond the render's, so the cap now stands 1.05 m over the coping (0.95 before); there the photograph's top and the render's now agree to 1-2 px (x 1080-1082 against 1081-1084). Measured in this picture against the return's own courses under it (about 22 px a 0.46 m course here, 25 px in the render), the cap reads about 0.94 m over the coping against the render's 0.64 m before; that excess beyond the plate's is left to this camera's re-fit. T-2748: read through the re-fitted camera (4.1 px RMS). The print's cap (two dark discs, the upper x 1229-1257 at y 106-114, the lower at y 120-128, an upright stem under them at x 1245) tops out at x 1243, y 106; the render's at x 1232, y 119. Net of the camera's own 6 px at the rear pinnacle beside it, the cap stands about 7 px (0.13 m) higher over the coping than built, near this camera's error; but it also stands 11 px further right, which the rear pinnacle (1.5 px across) does not explain. Moved in the model, 0.3 m less set-back behind the return's face moves the render's cap 9 px right, and 0.3 m further back along the return 11 px right: the plate, Taylor 2135 and the 1887 view fix its place along the return, and its set-back (0.6 m) is the reconstructed coordinate, so this print reads the cowl about 0.3 m nearer the return's face than built. Left open for the build (carried on T-2751). T-2811: built and ruled with the 1888 plate. Read alone, this print wants the cowl about 0.3 m nearer the face: at 0.3 m its cap centre stands at x 1241 against the print's 1242.5 and its top at y 108 against 106, so the 0.13 m height excess T-2748 measured was the set-back's (nearer the face raises the cap in this low view) and not the cap's. But the 1888 Glessner plate, whose re-fitted camera holds both return pinnacles to 1-4 px, put the cap where it was built (centre y 630.5 against its 629.5 at 0.6 m) and puts it 10.5 px off at 0.3 m. Both cameras see a move along the return almost as a change of set-back, so no place satisfies both short of fitting their residuals (0.75 m further back, 0.5 m deeper, the cap raised by amounts the two disagree on). The cowl is built at their least-squares set-back, 0.45 m (0.42 m fitted; the place along the return, 3.29 m fitted, stays 3.3 m; the cap's height stays 1.05 m): here the cap's centre stands at x 1236.5 and its top at y 111, 6 px and 5 px from the print, which is the two cameras' disagreement and no longer a difference any placement of the cowl removes.

T-2578: the hall stack stands over the coping beside the ventilator, where this picture shows sky; the stack should stop below the coping, the cowl pipe plausibly being its flue's termination (left for T-2580). T-2712: fixed — the hall stack now stops at 16.1 m, under the return's coping, and the render shows sky over the coping beside the cowl as the picture does; the cowl's pipe rises from the stack's top.
T-2578: the ventilator's pipe reads pale beside the granite, as the print shows it (the colour itself is reconstructed: the print is monochrome).

T-2713: this view's camera (T-1883's fit, 9.1 px RMS on six front controls) places the rear pinnacle about 60 px right of and 40 px below the photograph's, so the north return reads longer and falls more steeply in the render than in the print. It needs a re-fit on the pinnacle apexes as T-2579 did for the other views before the return and the cap can be judged here; the print is faint at the apexes, which is why this run did not take it. T-2748: fixed by the re-fit. The camera is now solved level on the three pinnacle apexes the print shows, the front's north arris and its lattice rows and southmost third-storey light (pixel aspect 0.885, see the camera's solve), and the rear pinnacle's apex projects at x 1312.5, y 145 against the print's 1311, 139: 1.5 px across and 6 px down, inside the reading of a faint apex. The north return's run from the arris to the rear pinnacle and its coping's fall now lie on the print's to a few pixels over their whole length.

T-2714: the checker band's units are pitched 0.28 m along their rows (0.336 m before), with 0.07 m of ground between neighbours, as the 1888 Keith plate lays them; the rows are unchanged. Not judged here: the band's units are below this print's grain at Keith's distance.

T-2748: with this camera now holding grade (T-1883's grade reading at the south corner lands within 1 px vertically), the stoop can be compared here for the first time. In the c. 1888 print the landing's pierced balustrade reads at x 915-960, y 910-960 against the render's 950-990, 885-925, and the arch under the flight is a low round-headed opening at x 910-937, y 1012-1032 (about 27 x 20 px) against the render's 952-985, 973-1035 (about 33 x 62 px). The stoop stands about 35 px further left (east or south of where it is built) and its arch is far lower than built. T-2812 ruled it (tools/keith_c1888_stoop_read.py; docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/a18-gh-1800-block-looking-sw-c1888-stoop.json): the print draws the loggia's front at its built width (the deck front 85 px against 80, the pierced parapet 40 against 40, its shadowed north side beside it) displaced as one block about 35-40 px left and down, and no level camera holds that block and the crown together: fitted on the crown, every camera leaves the loggia 32-41 px off across and 29-49 px off down; fitted on both, the crown goes to 20 px and T-1883's south-corner grade point to 10-42 px. Only an eye 5-6 m up fits both (7.7 px RMS), and the print's own horizon refuses it: Glessner's two identical window grids scale about y 986, where that eye's horizon is y 734. The 1888 plate (its level fits have the pedestals' arrises and caps in them, 4.6-5.4 px RMS) and the 1965 slide (the shafts' and south pedestal's silhouettes, 3.4 px, the pedestal caps predicted within 3-4 px) place the loggia, its deck and its stair as built, with the plan's deck 2.7 m out; the plate draws the arch's crown at y 1728 against the built 1724, its void 10-15 px inside the built outline in its shadowed reveal. What this print shows of the arch is its head over a light band at y 1032 in front of it; where the block is displaced, the built crown lands on the print's (y 1009-1011 against 1012). So this print cannot place the stoop: a 35 px move would be about 0.9 m out from the front or 1.4 m south along it against three readings that hold it, and the stoop is not moved.

T-2813: re-rendered with Keith's crown 0.16 m lower (the moulded course under the lattice 0.20 m deep where it was 0.36 m, the checker and head bands unmoved); its camera re-solved on the moved crown controls (4.11 to 4.60 px RMS, tools/keith_crown_resolve.py). Read again at the crown beside the previous render: the lattice, coping and pinnacles move a few pixels at this picture's scale and nothing it shows opens a difference; the verdict stands as it was (differs).

T-2876: re-rendered on the GLB in the tree, T-2845's loggia (0.6 m pedestals at the first-floor plan's place, each pair's shafts 0.36 m apart, the flight 1.8 m clear and the stoop 0.15 m south), and read again beside the previous render: the render changes only at the loggia and flight (x 770-1309, y 210-1053), the pairs and flight moving a few pixels at this print's scale. This print looks along the loggia's north flank, where the plate's rear row (inland-1888, T-2876) would stand beside the front pairs; at its grain the bays between the pairs read as dark openings and a rear shaft cannot be told from them, so it is not read here, and the build is to read it again. The verdict stands as it was found (differs), with nothing open on this record.

T-2881: re-rendered on the loggia with its rear row built (a pedestal 0.6 m square against the wall behind each front one, carrying a pair of turned shafts 0.39 m off the wall at a 0.28 m pitch, their radii 0.78 of the front's, under a paired capital; tools/keith_loggia_rear_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-rear-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 1027-1112, y 760-934); this print looks along the loggia's north flank, where the rear north pair now stands behind the front one, but its bays read as dark openings at this grain behind Glessner's front and the tree (T-2876), so the rear row is not read here. The verdict stands as it was (differs); settling it is T-2882's.

T-2882: re-rendered on the loggia with a respond on the wall behind each rear pair (a flat pier the rear pedestal's width, 0.25 m deep, from the pedestal's top to the ceiling; tools/keith_loggia_respond_read.py, docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/keith_house_1808_prairie/keith-loggia-respond-read.json), and read again beside the previous render and the picture: the render changes only at the loggia (x 1029-1122, y 761-883); this print looks along the loggia's north flank behind Glessner's front and the tree, where the bays read as dark openings (T-2876, T-2881), so the respond is not read here. VERDICT SETTLED (T-2882): every item on this record is fixed or not shown, with reasons, and none is open; what the print shows of Keith (the crown with its lattice, pinnacles and coping, the third storey's arcade, the north return's courses and the cowl over it, the stoop T-2812 ruled this print cannot place against the plate and the slide) reads as built, so the verdict is matches.

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
